description.narrative: A Gender-responsive diagnosis assessing the incidence, forms and drivers of informality of workers in informal employment conducted and validated by the national Tripartite Council (May 2023). Key diagnostics recommendations include (1) designing social protection in order to offer a collective route to formalising employment, i.e. by creating the right incentives for not just workers but also economic units to formalise; (2) Implementing inclusive labour policies and channels for social dialogue in a changing world of work; (3) Skilling and reskilling across the lifecycle through active labour market policies; (4) Ensuring coherence between social and labour policies to support redistribution of unpaid work. The diagnostics report was shared with the Institute for macro-economic studies and research under the President of Uzbekistan for further actions. The plan is to use the diagnostic results for the development of a National strategy on Transition from informal to formal economy. The Labour Force Survey (LFS) questionnaire of the Ministry of employment and poverty reduction has been amended by adding 7 new questions that were tested/piloted and adopted into the questionnaire enabling better measuring of informal employment (November 2022); The Road Map on further harmonization of the applied statistics tools in Uzbekistan in line with international labour statistics standards finalized and validated by the Tripartite Constituents improving the statistical measurement of informality (one of the items in DWCP roadmap). With the contribution of RBSA, the ILO organized a workshop for social partners and key national stakeholders on the methodology for a gender-responsive diagnostics of the scope, incidence and drivers of the informal economy and employment (November 2022). The ILO provided guidance at all stages of the diagnostic, provided comments and an in-depth review of the diagnostic report. With the contribution of RBSA, the ILO organized and delivered a training workshop for Uzbekistan tripartite constituents on international standards of labour statistics for household survey to measure informal employment and thus supports the inclusion of the new questions in the LFS questionnaires and then the identification, on this basis, of people in informal employment and in the informal sector in January 2023) Extensive policy advice, technical and expert support has been provided to the Uzbekistan Tripartite Constituents on the development of the Concept Note on the process of development of a National strategy on Transition from the Informal to the Formal economy (May 2022-November 2023). The Concept Note has been developed and agreed with social partners. The need for the development of a National strategy was acknowledged by the Government, practical steps pending.

description.narrative:
Public Employment Services (PES) in Uzbekistan has built the capacity to offer entrepreneurship training to jobseekers including young people, women, and returned migrant workers. SIYB training was delivered in May 2022. As a result, 11 government officials became certified SIYB trainers. The indicator 3.5.1. was achieved because the prescribed situation (i.e., the employment service designs and implements measures to improve the coverage or quality of services provided and workers covered, in particular to address evolving labour market needs in a rapidly changing world of work and in line with the follow-up plan of action on youth employment for the period 2020–30;) has occurred. Following the Governmental reform of December 2022, the functions related to the entrepreneurship development and support, have been shifted to the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction. To support the Ministry in execution of the new functions, the ILO implemented SIYB training for staff members of PES and public vocational training centres. The training has equipped them with necessary skills and knowledge to train persons willing to become entrepreneurs. As a result, 11 officials received SYIB Trainer Certificates May in 2023and are allowed to run SYIB trainings.
In addition to the SIYB training, the ILO implemented PES staff training to enhance their capacity to respond to jobseekers’ needs and expectations in 2022-2023. The first regional training in Samarkand brought together PES staff from Samarkand, Bukhara, Navoi, Syrdaria, Surkhandaria, Kashkadaria, Jizzakh and Tashkent regions (October 2022). The second regional training brought together PES staff of the Republic of Karakalpakstan and Khorezm region (March 2023). These training deepened the knowledge of the participants on adaptation of employment services to COVID-19 pandemic, career guidance for jobseekers, employment support for people with disabilities, examples of PES reforms, and digitalization of services.
The ILO also developed an internet-based learning platform which allow access to ILO training and learning materials including six training modules based on the Manual “PES and the Future of Work”.
